The UK AI Regulation White Paper proposes to address capability gaps among regulators by prioritizing the ongoing assessment of different capability needs across the regulatory landscape. It acknowledges that regulating AI effectively will require many regulators to acquire new skills and expertise, particularly in AI technology and its unique characteristics. The White Paper highlights potential capability gaps, including technical expertise in AI, understanding how AI use cases interact across multiple regulatory regimes, and market intelligence on AI technologies.

To address these gaps, the White Paper mentions several collaborative options, including:

1. Establishing a common pool of expertise to create best practices for supporting innovation through regulatory approaches.
2. Facilitating collaborative initiatives between regulators, which may include further supporting existing initiatives like the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF) to share skills and expertise.
3. Working collaboratively with key partners to leverage existing work on capability needs and to enhance knowledge sharing among regulators.

These approaches aim to ensure that regulators can effectively adapt to the emergence of AI use cases and work together to address common regulatory challenges.
